slides.14.questions.0.question: The Gallo Nero (Black Rooster) emblem is the symbol of which appellation?
slides.14.questions.0.explanation: The Black Rooster (Gallo Nero) is the official emblem of Chianti Classico DOCG, representing the historic core zone between Florence and Siena — higher quality than regular Chianti and requiring 100% Sangiovese.
slides.14.questions.1.question: What is the minimum ageing requirement for Brunello di Montalcino DOCG?
slides.14.questions.1.explanation: Brunello di Montalcino requires a minimum of 5 years' ageing (including 2 years in oak). The Riserva version requires 6 years — one of Italy's most demanding ageing requirements.
slides.14.questions.2.question: What are the main characteristics of Super Tuscan wines? (Multiple choice)
slides.14.questions.2.options.0: A. Use of non-traditional varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot
slides.14.questions.2.options.2: C. Born from innovative experiments in the 1970s–80s
slides.14.questions.2.explanation: Super Tuscans represent winemakers breaking the rules: using international varieties and initially only able to be labelled IGT, yet achieving outstanding quality. Sassicaia later earned its own DOC, becoming Italy's most iconic prestige wine.
slides.14.questions.3.question: What is Sangiovese's status in Italian viticulture?
slides.14.questions.3.options.1: B. Italy's most widely planted red grape variety
slides.14.questions.3.options.2: C. A newly introduced international variety
slides.14.questions.3.options.3: D. Mainly used for white wine
slides.14.questions.3.explanation: Sangiovese is Italy's most widely planted red grape. Beyond Tuscany, it is also found in Umbria, Marche, Emilia, and other central Italian regions.
slides.14.questions.4.question: Which of the following are Tuscan DOCG red wines? (Multiple choice)
slides.14.questions.4.explanation: Brunello di Montalcino, Chianti Classico, and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano are all Tuscan DOCGs. Barolo is a Piemonte DOCG and has no connection to Tuscany.
slides.15.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
quiz.0.question: What is Tuscany's most important red grape variety?
quiz.0.explanation: Sangiovese is the soul grape of Tuscany, covering over 90% of the region's plantings.
quiz.1.question: Which grape must Brunello di Montalcino be made from?
quiz.1.explanation: Brunello di Montalcino DOCG requires 100% Sangiovese (locally called Brunello).
quiz.2.question: Super Tuscans are typically labelled at which classification level?
quiz.2.explanation: Super Tuscans use international varieties or non-traditional blends, so they can only be labelled as Toscana IGT.
quiz.3.question: What is the emblem of Chianti Classico?
quiz.3.explanation: The Black Rooster (Gallo Nero) is the official emblem of Chianti Classico, representing the traditional core zone.
